cases.retention: Owner-managed role-memory card lifecycle; active/cold/archived/tombstone states remain explicit.
cases.deletion: Deletion and tombstoning are performed by role-memory card governance and remove retrievability.
cases.invalidation: Review, evidence, scope or version invalidation marks the card non-injectable until the owner re-accepts it.
cases.migration: Legacy role-memory SQLite cards remain in place; field normalization is applied without moving the store.

cases.retention: Runtime Memory owns fact TTL, session/run scope and eviction.
cases.deletion: Runtime Memory removes the fact and invalidates dependent usage/embedding entries.
cases.invalidation: Contradiction, stale evidence or scope mismatch invalidates the fact before retrieval.
cases.migration: Existing Runtime Memory state remains in its domain store; no forced single-database migration.

cases.retention: Timeline retention follows its owning session or run.
cases.deletion: Deleting the owning session/run removes or invalidates timeline state.
cases.invalidation: A replaced generation or invalidated episode makes the timeline stale.
cases.migration: Timeline records stay in Runtime Memory; schema changes are additive.

cases.retention: Episode retention is bounded by Runtime Memory lifecycle.
cases.deletion: Runtime Memory owns episode deletion and dependent index removal.
cases.invalidation: Lost execution context or contradiction invalidates the episode.
cases.migration: Episodes remain in Runtime Memory; retrieval indexes can be rebuilt from accepted evidence.

cases.retention: Candidate queue may persist beyond a session but is bounded by owner policy.
cases.deletion: Reject/delete removes the candidate or leaves an audit tombstone without accepted content.
cases.invalidation: Rejected, superseded or stale candidates are never promoted into retrieval.
cases.migration: Candidate records remain in the queue store and reference an accepted-memory target by identity.
cases.candidateGate: never retrievable or injectable before acceptance

cases.retention: Index lifetime follows the accepted source and embedding provider policy.
cases.deletion: Deleting an accepted source removes or rebuilds its vector entries.
cases.invalidation: Changed source digest, provider/model change or deleted source invalidates the index entry.
cases.migration: Embeddings are rebuildable derived data and are never the sole copy of memory.

cases.retention: Query receipts are transient and bounded by the request.
cases.deletion: No durable memory is created; transient query records may be discarded.
cases.invalidation: A changed source file invalidates the query result.
cases.migration: Native memory files remain read-only sources; no migration into another database is required.

cases.retention: Dreaming caches follow phase/storage policy and may be rebuilt from accepted sources.
cases.deletion: Reset/repair operations remove derived diary/cache artifacts without deleting accepted memory.
cases.invalidation: Cache input changes, duplicate repair or reset invalidates and rebuilds derived signals.
cases.migration: Dreaming remains a rebuildable derived cache; it is not migrated as accepted memory.

noDataLossMigration: embedding indexes and Dreaming caches are rebuildable
